content.overview: Article 323B empowers the appropriate Legislature by law to provide for the adjudication or trial by tribunals of disputes, complaints or offences with respect to matters specified in the article (including tax, foreign exchange, industrial and labour, land reforms, urban ceiling, elections to local bodies, foodstuffs, and other matters as listed). The law may provide for hierarchy, powers and procedure, and may exclude the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court under Article 136 — subject to the Constitution and judicial interpretation on the scope of exclusion and the competence of the Legislature.
content.glance: Appropriate Legislature may create tribunals for specified matters (tax, labour, land reforms, local elections, etc.). Hierarchy, procedure, and limited court exclusion (except Art 136) — subject to constitutional limits.
content.study:
Article 323B (42nd Amendment) extends the tribunal model beyond service matters to a list of subjects:
- Tax, foreign exchange/export/import, industrial and labour disputes, land reforms, urban property ceiling, elections to Parliament/State Legislature are **not** the only items — the article lists specific heads including local-body elections, foodstuffs, and others as enumerated.
- **Appropriate Legislature**: Parliament or State Legislature according to the distribution of legislative power for the subject.
- Same structural features as 323A: hierarchy, procedure, possible exclusion of courts except SC under Art 136, subject to basic-structure/judicial-review limits.

Examination: list of matters; appropriate Legislature; contrast Art 323A (services only, Parliament only); ouster limits.

sections.heading: Key elements
sections.body:
1. Appropriate Legislature may by law provide tribunals for matters listed in Art 323B.
2. Includes tax, labour/industrial, land reforms, local elections, and other enumerated heads.
3. Hierarchy, powers, procedure; possible exclusion of courts except SC under Art 136 (subject to constitutional limits).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 323B provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 323B empowers the appropriate Legislature by law to provide for the adjudication or trial by tribunals of disputes, complaints or offences with respect to matters specified in the article, including taxation, foreign exchange, industrial and labour disputes, land reforms, ceiling on urban property, elections to local authorities, production and distribution of foodstuffs, and other listed heads. The law may provide for the hierarchy, jurisdiction, powers and procedure of such tribunals and may exclude the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court under Article 136, subject to the Constitution and limits on ouster of judicial review.

examTips: Tribunals for listed non-service matters; appropriate Legislature; contrast 323A.

keyTakeaways: Art 323B: tribunals for other specified matters.
